site.title: Production AI Patterns
site.tagline: A pattern language for AI that has to survive contact with production.
site.description: Named, reusable patterns for the architectural decisions that actually determine whether an AI system survives production traffic — context, cost, reliability, observability, and security.

articles.title: The Cost Gate
articles.hook: Inference spend can spike orders of magnitude faster than traffic. The cost gate wraps high-cost model calls in a budget-aware gate that degrades gracefully instead of blowing up the billing dashboard at 2 AM.

articles.title: Deaf at the Wheel
articles.hook: Model health ≠ outcome health. Your AI dashboards instrument the call, not the consequence.

articles.title: Circuit Breaker for Model Inference
articles.hook: When the model endpoint starts returning 500s or timing out, you need to stop hammering it. The circuit breaker adapted for LLM and embedding serving — with half-open recovery, fallback chains, and SLO-aware trip thresholds.

articles.title: Reading the Pattern Language
articles.hook: How this catalog is organized, what a 'pattern' means here, and how to navigate from symptom to solution when your system is breaking in production.

articles.title: The Unbounded Memory Trap
articles.hook: Accumulated context isn't a superpower; it is an unpatched attack surface.

articles.title: Quarantined Feedback Is Not a Retraining Problem
articles.hook: Your model isn't learning from the world. It's learning from its own shadow in your warehouse.

articles.title: Predictive Token-Budget Circuit Breaker
articles.hook: Cost governance is not an API gateway rate-limiting problem; it is a stateful graph execution gate.

articles.title: Your Budget Is a Receipt
articles.hook: A monthly budget is a postmortem tool dressed up as a guardrail — real cost governance for LLM workflows lives in the request path, not the invoice.

articles.title: The Infinite Wallet
articles.hook: AI agents do not crash; they spend, and traditional reliability patterns are entirely blind to the financial blast radius of a probabilistic infinite loop.

articles.title: The Fungibility Trap
articles.hook: Standard infrastructure assumes requests are fungible; probabilistic AI systems shatter this assumption, requiring cost governance to shift from the network layer to the semantic layer.

articles.title: Stop Retrying Your Agents: Bounded Cascade Degradation for LLM Pipelines
articles.hook: Standard retries make LLM agent pipelines worse — each retry inflates context, burns tokens, and lowers success probability.

articles.title: Bleeding Tokens Silently
articles.hook: Financial governance for production AI is not an accounting audit; it is a real-time edge control-plane problem requiring synchronous token-bucket circuit breaking before inference executes.

articles.title: Feedback Eats Itself
articles.hook: A feedback loop that improves your aggregate metrics is probably narrowing your capability distribution — and the dashboard will never tell you.

articles.title: Context-Filtered Gateway Decomposition
articles.hook: Long context windows aren't a feature; they're an expensive operational state leak.

articles.title: Valid JSON Is Not a Valid Answer
articles.hook: Structured outputs solved the parsing problem and quietly hid the correctness problem — a schema guarantees shape, never truth.

articles.title: Agents Don't Retry, They Repeat
articles.hook: An agent that re-issues a timed-out tool call is not retrying — it is acting twice, and your retry policy never saw it happen.

articles.title: The Lethal Trifecta Is an Architecture Bug
articles.hook: Prompt injection is not a filtering problem you can tune away; it is a capability-composition problem you have to design away.

articles.title: Prompt Regression Gates in CI
articles.hook: Prompt changes are not config changes; they are model behavior changes that need automated gates to catch silent regressions before they reach production.

articles.title: Prefix-Cache-Aligned Prompts
articles.hook: Prefix caching saves 90% of compute on repeated contexts, but only if your prompt structure groups static content at the start. Prompt design that ignores cache boundaries is leaving 10× latency and 90% cost on the table.

articles.title: Unbounded Concurrency Explosion
articles.hook: Inference endpoints are not databases; they do not scale linearly with concurrency. The N-th concurrent request pays an exponential latency tax, and your system will not realize it until the model is thrashing.
